title: Retirees back at work and provisional hires: the Charter limits
question: What does the Charter allow when a retired City employee works again, and how long may a provisional appointment last?
finding: Charter A8.511(c)(2) lets a retired member work in a post requiring special skills for no more than 120 working days or 960 hours, whichever is greater, in one fiscal year, and bars using the retiree to replace a permanent civil-service employee. Section 10.105 caps provisional appointments at three years unless the Board approves a renewal.
how: Sections A8.511, A8.587-10 and 10.105 read from the Charter text; quotations checked word for word.
limits: Other retirement plans in Appendix A8 carry their own employment sections; the payroll does not say which plan a person retired under, so the limit that applies to any one person cannot be read from the payroll. "Whichever is greater" means a person working long days may pass 960 hours within 120 days and stay inside the limit.

rows.rule: A retired member may be employed in a non-teaching post requiring special skills for up to 120 working days or 960 hours, whichever is greater, in a fiscal year, and keep the pension; the work must not replace a permanent civil-service employee.
rows.quote: for not to exceed 120 working days or 960 hours, whichever is greater, in any one fiscal year and may be paid for that employment
rows.verdict: Confirmed: the limit runs on the City fiscal year

rows.rule: The same section bars using a returning retiree in place of a permanent civil-service employee.
rows.quote: Furthermore, this employment shall not replace a permanent civil service employee.

rows.rule: Members of the plan in A8.587 who retire may serve on a City board or commission and be paid for it for up to 120 working days or 960 hours a fiscal year.
rows.quote: provided said service does not exceed 120 working days or 960 hours per fiscal year

rows.rule: A provisional appointment (where no eligible list exists) may not exceed three years; renewal needs the Board of Supervisors and a Human Resources certification that examinations could not be held.
rows.quote: Provisional appointments for classified positions for which no eligible list exists shall not exceed three years.
